description: A broad extraction of a macOS acquisition (an Expert Witness, sparse, VMDK or UDIF image, a raw APFS container or HFS+ volume, a raw disk with an Apple GPT partition, or a folder that is the root of a macOS volume): the pinned mac_apt 1.33.2 runs a plugin set over it in the input mode the object shows (FAST unless the target names its plugins) and writes its database, CSV files and log under mac_apt/. mac_apt exits 0 after errors it has logged, so the run reads its own log for one outcome per plugin (plugins.tsv: parsed, empty, unsupported or failed) and says complete only when mac_apt exited 0, the log has its start line and its finish line, every plugin the target names is parsed or empty and no error line or traceback sits outside a plugin; FAST and ALL can never be complete because the plugins they expand to are not listed by anything read here. mac_apt was never installed or run to build this recipe: its argument shape and the texts of the start, plugin start, plugin end, plugin exception and finish log lines were read from its v1.33.2 source (GitHub, 2026-11-04); the prefix of a log line, the wording of an empty or unsupported plugin and the per-plugin file names were not, and empty and unsupported rest on an assumed wording. coverage.json is written first (partial) and replaced whole at the end; a run never writes over an earlier run. On arm64, where mac_apt is not installed (its statx helper stops at import), detect exits 1 with the packaging reason. The output is the examined system's own content: coverage.json marks every file it wrote under secret_bearing.
object: macOS disk image, volume or mounted folder
exclusions: what no plugin of the pinned mac_apt release parses: those files stay in the source, unread by this extraction
deleted records beyond what a plugin reads itself (SQLite free pages, WAL): nothing is carved
an encrypted volume: no password is passed here, and what mac_apt does without one was never observed (the tool macos_triage takes a sealed password file)
UAC, Velociraptor and AFF4 inputs: this recipe does not detect them (the tool macos_triage takes them with an input type the caller names)
the plugins a FAST or ALL set expands to are not listed by anything read here, so a plugin that never started cannot be told from one that was not meant to
a plugin the log does not account for as parsed or empty: see plugins.tsv
covers: What mac_apt's plugins parse from the acquisition: its database, the per-plugin files of the CSV format and its log, kept whole under mac_apt/, with plugins.tsv holding the outcome of each plugin the log names or the target asked for. A plugin that finds nothing is empty only by an assumed wording of its log lines, a plugin that does not take the operating-system version is unsupported only by an assumed wording, and parsed is not a count of records; a plugin that failed, whose end the log does not show, or that never started is not covered, however many others wrote. The program runs in a process group of its own with a time limit of its own (--max-seconds, default 14100 seconds, under the 14400 of the limit): one that does not finish is ended with everything it started, what it wrote is kept, and the run says partial or failed, never complete; a stop signal ends the program and its children before the recipe ends. A run never writes over an earlier run's output. The output is the examined system's own content (a sensitive output).
